mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS is below its 5-year moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% in the next month signals labor market strength, boosting corporate profits and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.0% in the next month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not higher than average when UNRATE does not fall below 5.0% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concomitant easing (FEDFUNDS decline) and rising demand (GDPC1 growth) create favorable conditions for equity investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases while GDPC1 increases over the next month
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the FEDFUNDS/GDPC1 relationship does not align with the predicted positive correlation (IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for 30 days indicates a tightening monetary cycle, raising discount rates on equities and compressing forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS is in tightening (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Accelerated demand growth (GDPC1) outpacing supply growth (INDPRO) signals healthy economic expansion, boosting market confidence and short-term S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth exceeds INDPRO growth by 2% over the next week
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns are not higher than average when the GDPC1/INDPRO growth differential does not meet the threshold (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) combined with stable monetary policy creates market uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises while FEDFUNDS remains stable over the next quarter
regime_hint: labor market weakening under stable rates
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE rises and FEDFUNDS is stable (IC > 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing corporate profits and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60d returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is rising (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Easing monetary policy (FEDFUNDS decline) offsets rising unemployment (UNRATE) by lowering discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases while UNRATE increases by 0.5% over the next month
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns are not positively correlated with the FEDFUNDS/UNRATE relationship (IC < 0.03).
